title: A British Officer in the Balkans
subtitle: The Account of a Journey through Dalmatia, Montenegro, Turkey in Austria, Magyarland, Bosnia and Hercegovina
short_title: A British Officer in the Balkans
summary: Major Percy E. Henderson (born 1852), a retired officer of the Indian Army who wrote as “Selim,” describes travels with his wife in the western Balkans a few years before 1909, when Bosnia and Hercegovina were under Austrian rule. They go down the Dalmatian coast from Fiume to Spalato, Ragusa, and the Bocche di Cattaro, drive up to Cetinje in Montenegro, and then go inland to Mostar and Sarajevo, where they stay for some time. He writes about markets, festivals, dervishes, the government carpet and cigarette factories, costumes, and the life of Muslim women. A summer visit to the Hungarian countryside and Budapest, with a bull-fight, makes Part III. In Part IV they return to Bosnia and travel by carriage and on horseback through Jajce, Travnik, the Zelengora mountains, and the Drina valley. The fifty photographs were taken by Mrs. Henderson.

notes_on_text: The book’s map is missing from the scanned copy (a photocopy made in 1989 to replace a worn volume) and from the other copy at the Internet Archive.
The photographs are reproduced from that photocopy, so they are less clear than in the printed book.
The chapter summaries are printed under each chapter title; the contents here give the chapter titles only.
